messages:
alisha: quick sync - need final rules for header-based routing. two competing signals: signed auth headers (X-Auth-Tenant / X-Auth-Sig) vs user-agent app fingerprints. goal: avoid quota misattribution and spoofing while allowing gradual sdk rollouts.

matt: auth headers first. UA is unreliable and trivial to spoof.

irene: agreed in principle, but many legacy mobile SDKs don't set auth tenant yet. we need a designed fallback so we don't break users.

sam: proposal: prioritized matcher chain: 1) signed auth header -> tenant route; 2) verified UA fingerprint -> tenant route but only for lightweight routes; 3) default -> hosted. Also enforce lower rate caps for UA-derived routing.

alisha: sketch config (ordering matters):
```
matchers:
  - id: header_signed
    when: header_exists("X-Auth-Tenant") && verify_sig("X-Auth-Sig")
    action: route(tenant_from_header)
  - id: ua_fingerprint_light
    when: ua_in(known_apps) && route_category in ["generate","embed"]
    action: route(tenant_from_ua) ; limits: 50r/s per-tenant
  - id: fallback_hosted
    action: route(hosted_pool)
```

irene: Console UX note: show "routing=inferred_by_ua (unverified)" on traces and in the per-request table so support and customers see why a request landed on a tenant. add a link to raw headers.

matt: ops question - verify signature at the edge or call control plane? Prefer edge verify with cached public keys (short TTL) to keep latency low. fallback to control-plane verify if key missing.

security-bot: risky to permit UA fallback broadly. only allow for read/low-privilege paths (inference, embeddings). never for admin or billing endpoints. log all UA-derived route events with reason and partial headers (redact PII).

sam: telemetry plan: emit routing.source=[signed_header, ua_inferred, default], routing.verified=true/false, routing.target=[tenant:ID, hosted]. emit per-tenant counters for ua_inferred so we can alert if it spikes.

alisha: rollout plan: feature-flag header.routing.v3 -> canary: 1% with header_signed enforced but ua_fallback disabled. check metrics 24h. enable ua_fallback 2% canary for lightweight endpoints, monitor spoofing and quota deltas, then step to 10% and 25% if safe. emergency kill-switch to disable ua fallback globally.

matt: i'll add signature verification and key-cache in gateway (pr queued). keys rotate via control plane; gateway caches public keys with revocation TTL.

sam: i'll add metrics and an alert: if ua_inferred > 1% of tenant_requests for any tenant -> pager. also emit a per-request audit event to the sec audit stream.

irene: i'll add badges and a routing_source column in the Console request viewer, plus a small tooltip explaining "inferred = based on UA fingerprint, unverified".

alisha: ops runbook items: how to interpret audit tags, steps to disable UA fallback, how to surface suspected spoofing incidents. add step to compare quota billing groups vs auth-routed counts.

matt: ops-bot: staging build passed.

ops-bot: staging/gateway build 2026-03-18T12:02Z succeeded :white_check_mark:

alisha: owners: matt (gateway verification + key cache), sam (telemetry + alerts), irene (console badges + traces), matt+security (key rotation + audit retention). i'll draft the runbook and share.

sam: created ticket INFRA-5899 for metrics + alerting.

matt: PR #4612 up for gateway changes.

irene: dashboard PR linked: https://console.internal/p/boards/289

alisha: final asks: keep an eye on quota mismatches after canary. if we see large discrepancies between tenant usage in auth-routed vs billing groups, pause. emergency env var to force-disable UA fallback exists and is ops-only.

matt: noted, will include env override and RBAC.

alisha: thanks team. closing thread for now; will reopen if telemetry shows unexpected spoofing or quota drift.
